findings.title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
findings.body: The unsubscribe action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then unconditionally calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!`. For any user who has not previously visited/read the topic (or whose topic_users row was deleted) there is no TopicUser row and `find_by` returns nil, so the first comparison raises NoMethodError on nil and the user sees a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. New users on a topic they have never opened will hit this on the very first click from the email. The action should use `TopicUser.find_or_create_by(...)` (or the existing `TopicUser.change` helper which already creates the row on miss) and otherwise guard against nil.

findings.title: GET-based state change with no auth token enables CSRF unsubscribe
findings.body: The unsubscribe endpoint is GET-only and the URL it generates (`{base}/t/{slug}/{id}/unsubscribe`) contains no per-user authentication token, unlike Discourse's other email-triggered endpoints (e.g. `email/unsubscribe/:key`, `users/password-reset/:token`, `users/activate-account/:token`). Any third-party site can force a logged-in Discourse user to be unsubscribed/muted from any topic simply by referencing the URL (e.g. as an ``, hidden link, or redirect). Once the user lands on it, `tu.save!` mutates their notification level with no confirm step. The action should either be POST/PUT (so Rails' CSRF token applies) or the link in the email should carry a signed/email-token like the existing global unsubscribe (`email#unsubscribe`) does.

findings.title: No explicit guardian check before mutating state
findings.body: Before doing `tu.save!` the controller relies on `TopicView.new` raising to deny access, but there is no explicit `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or equivalent). If `TopicView.new` ever stops raising for some category/PM edge case, or if a later refactor changes that, the action will happily downgrade a TopicUser row for a topic the user is not entitled to interact with. Add an explicit guardian check (matching the pattern used by `clear_pin`/`re_pin`/`mute` in the same controller) before mutating user state.

findings.title: mailing_list_notify omits unsubscribe_url, breaking the feature for mailing-list users
findings.body: `send_notification_email` is shared between the per-user notification path and `mailing_list_notify`, but `mailing_list_notify` (lines 146-159) builds its opts hash without `unsubscribe_url:` while the other callers now pass `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`. As a result users in mailing-list mode still get the old footer with only the global preferences link and no per-topic unsubscribe link, which is inconsistent with the stated goal of this PR and means the new i18n text "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})" is never shown for these emails.

findings.title: Misspelled property leaks to template handlebars
findings.body: The CP is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i' after Notific). The template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) refers to it as `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` so it works, but the misspelling will bite anyone who tries to grep, rename, or reuse it, and Ember will warn about unknown handlebars bindings the moment either side is corrected. Rename to `stopNotificationsText` and update the template accordingly.

findings.title: New unsubscribe behavior is not actually asserted
findings.body: The diff only adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the existing `message_with_unsubscribe` let-block, but no expectation is added that this URL ends up in the rendered body. The "unsubscribe link" context only checks that the user preferences URL appears; there is no test asserting that `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the `unsubscribe_link` i18n key and surfaces in the body/html_part. Given the i18n string was changed and the unsubscribe_url plumbing is brand new, a regression here would silently produce emails with the global-preferences-only footer again.

findings.title: No controller spec for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: There is no topics_controller_spec coverage for the new `unsubscribe` action: nil-TopicUser case, slug mismatch redirect, the regular->muted vs tracking/watching->regular branch, permission denial, and that the rendered view is `topics/show`. Combined with the silent `tu.save!` and the fact that this action is the entry point for every per-topic unsubscribe email, a regression here will only be caught in production.
